newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan believes can settle insurance row with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Japan believes can settle insurance row with U.S..

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday that he believes the United States and Japan can settle their dispute over Japan's insurance market by a newly-set December 15 deadline.

Speaking at a news conference after meeting with U.S. officials in Washington while attending a meeting of the G7 industrialised nations and the IMF, Kubo said the two sides had confirmed their commitment to settle the dispute.

The United States is pressing Japan to open its primary insurance markets but wants the so-called "third sector" in which foreign firms have a strong foothold, from being opened to Japanese insurers in the interim.
The dispute has become a major trade irritant between the two countries. They had originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute but agreed this week to extend it to December 15.
